A.explanation: This is the extension if the spring constants were added as $k = 6.0 + 4.0 = 10 \text{ N cm}^{-1}$, which applies to parallel springs, not the series arrangement shown.

B.explanation: This is too small because it is less than the extension of the softer $4.0 \text{ N cm}^{-1}$ spring alone, which must stretch by $80/4.0 = 20 \text{ cm}$.

C.explanation: This is about half the true total and would result from assuming the 80 N load is shared between the springs, whereas in series each spring carries the full 80 N.

D.explanation: The total extension is the sum of the two series extensions: $80/6.0 + 80/4.0 = 13.3 + 20 = 33.3 \text{ cm}$.

Recall Hooke's law as $F = kx$, so the extension of each spring is $x = F/k$ with $F = 80 \text{ N}$ for both springs.
Calculate the $6.0 \text{ N cm}^{-1}$ extension and the $4.0 \text{ N cm}^{-1}$ extension separately in $\text{cm}$, then add them to get the composite extension.
walkthrough: The diagram shows a series combination because the springs are joined end-to-end with the 80 N load below them, so each spring experiences the full $F = 80 \text{ N}$ and their extensions add.
Use Hooke's law $F = kx$ rearranged to $x = F/k$ for each spring separately, keeping $k$ in $\text{N cm}^{-1}$ so $x$ is directly in $\text{cm}$.
For the upper spring: $x_1 = 80/6.0 = 13.3 \text{ cm}$ to 3 significant figures.
Add for series: $x = x_1 + x_2 = 13.3 + 20 = 33.3 \text{ cm}$, which rounds to about $33 \text{ cm}$ with the given data.
